description: Declares the common layer contract: which agents and skills are provided by templates/common/, their versions, and override governance rules. Variants inherit these via new-project.ts and may declare overrides in their variant.json. Country-scoped skills (k-law/k-dart/k-kosis, tracked in workspace-schema.json country_scoped_assets) and variant-scoped skills (tracked in variant_scoped_skills, living in templates/co-*/skills/) are deliberately out of this contract. The common_platform_skill_exclusions section records platform skills deliberately outside this inventory (L0-only operator skills, claude-only tools, variant-scoped skills); every skill dir under the templates/common/.{claude,gemini,agents,codex}/skills/ mirrors must be listed here, in common_skills/common_platform_skills, or documented as an exclusion (T-20260924-002 full-inventory ruling).

Use when: after scaffolding a new variant, on a periodic cadence (every 5 new variants or quarterly, whichever first), or on-demand when asked to check for or reduce context.md duplication across variants.

project-resync.description: Full bidirectional sync cycle for Projects/co-* instances: provenance-audit uncommitted content, sync each project to its GitHub remote, selectively promote reusable work back into templates/L0, run the root /sync, upgrade projects from their variant templates, and land upgrade PRs. Use when: user says "project-resync", "resync projects", "resync the project fleet", "sync project cycle", or asks to sync/backport/upgrade the Projects/* fleet. Distinct from the `sync` skill (single-repo commit→PR pipeline): this is the whole-fleet, bidirectional cycle.

Use when: the weekly analytics cadence fires (the 02:30 ticket runner may invoke it), the user says "skill-graph analytics", "fleet skill graph", "skill graph report", or asks which skills the project fleet carries, which root skills never reached projects, whether any agent or skill is orphaned, or what changed fleet-wide since last week.

variant-feature.description: Add features to an existing variant template. Use when: extending a variant with new agents, skills, scripts, or documentation.

platform_settings.description: Classifies .claude/settings.json and .gemini/settings.json keys into tiers. SSOT for platform settings parity governance. Tier definitions: shared=required in both, claude_only=Claude Code exclusive (absent from .gemini is correct), gemini_only=Gemini CLI exclusive (absent from .claude is correct). Note: Antigravity (VS Code extension) shares .gemini/settings.json but does NOT fire hooks. SCOPE RULING (T-20260926-022, 2026-09-26): the tier model is DELIBERATELY scoped to the two settings.json-shaped surfaces (.claude/.gemini). .codex uses config.toml (no TOML merge machinery; template-side changes reach only new projects — ADR-0076 D7 precedent, upgrade-policy v1.16.0 D6/D7), .agents is a read-only skill-mirror surface with no settings file, and .hermes onboarding is config-driven (`context_file_max_chars`, `trusted_project_dirs` — ADR-0088), not settings.json-shaped. Functional-equivalence parity for those three is governed by their own platform sections, not by this tier table; revisit only if a settings-shaped surface appears on another platform.

shared.description: Settings that both Claude Code and Antigravity support with the same intent. Must be present in both .claude/settings.json and .gemini/settings.json.
